page: The Vultr voc-m-8c-64gb-1600s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance engineered for memory-intensive and data-heavy enterprise workloads. It is powered by dedicated AMD EPYC processors running on the x86_64 architecture, configured with 4 physical cores and 8 threads to provide 8 dedicated vCPUs clocked at 2.0 GHz. The processor architecture includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and a 32 MB shared L3 cache, complemented by standard instruction set extensions such as AVX, AES, and SHA-NI.

Hardware provisioning features 64.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU allocation ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is addressed via an integrated 1600 GB local NVMe SSD, providing high-capacity local disk space with minimal I/O overhead. The platform includes one complimentary public IPv4 address and omits hardware-accelerated graphics processing units, centering resource allocation entirely on memory density and localized storage throughput.

Benchmark evaluations reveal top-tier single-core CPU execution, achieving a stress-ng single-core score of 3135.58, alongside a balanced multi-core score of 24996.08. Synthetic benchmarks reflect solid memory capabilities, showing top-quartile performance in uncached large-block read operations at 258.36 GB/sec and write operations at 152.63 GB/sec, corroborated by a PassMark memory score of 2868.01. Geekbench metrics demonstrate dependable general processing with a 1489 single-core and 7550 multi-core score. Redis set throughput reaches 19.1 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput registers at 7.39 GB/sec. Weaknesses emerge in heavier algorithmic execution, such as medium-tier 7B LLM prompt processing yielding 21.78 tokens per second, illustrating limits in non-accelerated machine learning contexts.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance maximizes value through its tight coupling of dense RAM and high-capacity NVMe media without requiring detached block storage attachments. The dedicated core model avoids resource contention typical of shared infrastructure. This instance profile is structurally matched to large in-memory caching nodes, relational databases, enterprise analytics engines, and transactional processing backends.
description: The Vultr voc-m-8c-64gb-1600s-amd is a memory-optimized cloud server built for data-demanding infrastructure requirements. Equipped with an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor, it delivers 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores running at 2.0 GHz, coupled with 32 MB of L3 cache. Memory provisioning is substantial, offering 64.0 GB of RAM configured at an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Local storage is provided through a bundled 1600 GB NVMe SSD, and networking includes one complimentary public IPv4 address, with zero dedicated GPU accelerators present. Benchmark data confirms top-tier single-core compute performance and strong uncached memory read and write bandwidth in the upper 25th percentile, supporting up to 19.1 million Redis set operations per second. However, compute-bound workloads like larger language model processing highlight the boundaries of CPU-only execution. The configuration provides balanced resource density for in-memory caching platforms, mid-scale relational databases, and data processing backends.
